articles.title: Diagnostic Validity of Ultrasound Imaging After Injection Into the Peroneal Tendon Sheath for Detecting Pseudo-Pouch Formation in Recurrent Peroneal Tendon Dislocation.
articles.authors: Nishimura A, Nakazora S, Senga Y, Ito N, Hasegawa M
articles.population: Patients with surgically confirmed recurrent peroneal tendon dislocation and symptomatic controls without dislocation
articles.sample_size: 23 ankles with recurrent peroneal tendon dislocation and 11 control ankles
articles.outcomes: Sensitivity, specificity and interobserver agreement for detecting pseudo-pouch formation using ultrasound-guided fluid injection compared with MRI, with intraoperative findings as reference standard
articles.take_home: Ultrasound imaging with fluid injection into the tendon sheath detected pseudo-pouches in all 21 cases where they were found at surgery, whilst MRI only detected them in 38% of cases. This technique may help diagnose recurrent peroneal tendon dislocation when the tendon dislocation cannot be reproduced during physical examination.

articles.title: Hindfoot Varus Is Not Universally Present in Muller-Weiss Disease: A Clinical and Radiographic Analysis.
articles.authors: Bai W, Cheng C, Zheng H, Li Y, Zhu Y, Shen G
articles.sample_size: 103 patients (160 feet), mean age 58.3 years, 92.2% women
articles.outcomes: Hindfoot alignment measured using Saltzman view, clinical hindfoot alignment angle, Kite angle, and lateral Meary-Tomeno angle
articles.take_home: Hindfoot varus is not a universal feature of Muller-Weiss disease, with 52.5% of patients showing non-varus alignment. Clinical hindfoot appearance and Kite angle measurements help predict hindfoot alignment and should guide individualised treatment planning.

articles.title: Gracilis tendon harvesting using the posterior approach for anatomical ankle ligament reconstruction: A rapid and reliable technique with minimal neurological complications.
articles.authors: Khvesyuk M, Nogier A, van Rooij F, Beaudet P
articles.population: Adults with chronic ankle instability undergoing anatomic ankle ligament reconstruction
articles.outcomes: Donor site morbidity, neurological complications, and patient-reported discomfort at follow-up
articles.take_home: Gracilis tendon harvesting using a posterior approach for ankle ligament reconstruction is safe, with only one patient experiencing nerve-related symptoms and five experiencing temporary donor-site discomfort. Most patients had no complications from the harvesting procedure.
